chunks: From him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who insulted another man without making an accusation of zinā, but alluded against him. Is he to be flogged? He said: “Upon him is taʿzīr.”

key_terms.بِغَيْرِ قَذْفٍ: without an explicit accusation of illicit sexual misconduct
key_terms.تَعْزِيرٌ: a discretionary disciplinary punishment determined by the judge or authority
key_terms.فَعَرَّضَ بِهِ: he spoke allusively against him or insinuated something about him
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: he is given the punishment of flogging

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone insults another person indirectly without explicit qadhf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning insulting speech that falls short of explicit qadhf. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that such a person is not subject to the fixed hadd punishment of flogging, but rather to taʿzīr, a discretionary disciplinary punishment.
